feeds.title: Chinese American Eyes
feeds.description: The website https://chimericaneyes.blogspot.com/ is a blog that showcases the work of Chinese American visual artists. It was created by Alex Jay, a writer and art historian. The blog features posts on a variety of artists, from well-known figures like Yun Gee to lesser-known artists like Mann Fong Lowe. Each post includes images of the artist's work, as well as information about the artist's life and career.

feeds.title: Museum of Chinese in America
feeds.description: Since its founding in 1980, MOCA has celebrated the living history of the Chinese experience in America by preserving and presenting the 200-year history, heritage, culture, and diverse experiences of American communities of Chinese descent. The museum strives to be responsive to the moment; tell nuanced and unexpected stories; spotlight politically conscious issues; and provide a platform for open dialogue and dynamic programs.

feeds.title: Is everybody having a good time?
feeds.description: Is everybody having a good time? is journaling of the life of a struggling artist/photographer in San Francisco.

feeds.title: Omnivore's Cookbook
feeds.description: Maggie Zhu write about modern chinese cooking - including street food, family recipes, and restaurant dishes. She takes a less labor-intensive approach while maintaining the taste and look of the dish. She is originally from Beijing, and now cook from her Austin, Texas kitchen.

feeds.title: The Woks of Life
feeds.description: The Woks of Life is a food blog run by a family of four. They share recipes for Chinese and Asian food, as well as tips on cooking, ingredients, and culture. The blog has over 200 recipes, including classics like kung pao chicken and mapo tofu, as well as more obscure dishes like zhajiangmian and jianbing. They also have a comprehensive glossary of Chinese ingredients, as well as travel guides to China and other parts of Asia.

feeds.title: Chandavkl's Blog
feeds.description: Chandavkl's Blog is about Menuism Chinese Restaurant Articles Discussing Chinese Food in the Context of Chinese-American History, Demographics and Culture.

feeds.title: Bicultural Mama Blog
feeds.description: Maria Wen Adcock is a freelance writer and the creator of the award-winning BiculturalMama.com, a parenting blog for bicultural families with a focus on Asian culture. She currently serves as Editor and Board Member for Multicultural Kid Blogs.

feeds.title: Chinese-American Planning Council
feeds.description: Founded in 1965, CPC is a social services organization that creates positive social change. They empower Asian American, immigrant, and low-income communities in New York City by ensuring they have equitable access to the resources and opportunities needed to thrive. Chinese-American Planning Council's mission is to promote the social and economic empowerment of Chinese American, immigrant, and low-income communities.

feeds.title: Chinese Healthy Cooking
feeds.description: Chinese Healthy Cooking blog features simple and easy everyday Chinese cooking recipes and tips by Ling. Ling is a Silicon Valley mom with three kids on the cusp of adulthood, she leads a dynamic life. Beyond her culinary pursuits, she's passionate about rowing, photography, reading, cycling, spending quality time with friends, and occasionally venting about her children. To fuel her various interests and hobbies, she works as a pediatric oncology pharmacist, all while juggling the responsibilities of parenthood.

feeds.title: Curated Kitchenware Blog
feeds.description: You may have seen these video recipes on YouTube or Facebook and now you can find the free printable recipes here at Curated Kitchenware Blog. Ad-Free website experience to help you get in and out of the kitchen faster.

feeds.title: Fly by Jing Blog
feeds.description: Fly By Jing Blog shares Thoughtfully crafted recipes to fire up Sichuan flavors at home, conversations with culinary leaders and inspired creatives, and big announcements from Team Jing find it all here.

feeds.title: 3Jamigos
feeds.description: 3Jamigos is a blog about food and recipes created by an Asian-American family who enjoys eating, cooking, and traveling together. The blog offers interesting insights into their cooking heritage, with recipes, ingredients, and techniques to help readers learn and appreciate different cultures. Whether you're looking for meal inspiration or love to explore new culinary territories, 3Jamigos is the perfect blog for you.

feeds.title: Kristina Wong Blog
feeds.description: Kristina Wong is a Doris Duke Artist Award winner, Guggenheim Fellow and a Pulitzer Prize finalist in Drama. She's a performance artist, comedian, actor and writer who has been presented internationally across North America, the UK, Hong Kong and Africa. She's been a guest on late night shows on NBC, Comedy Central and FX. She starred in her own pilot presentation with Lionsgate for truTV. Her commentaries have appeared on American Public Media's Marketplace, PBS, VICE, Jezebel, Playgirl Magazine, Huffington Post and CNN.

feeds.title: Chinese American Museum in Washington, DC
feeds.description: The Chinese American Museum's mission is to advance the understanding, knowledge, and appreciation of the Chinese American experience, by highlighting the history, culture, spirit, and contributions of Chinese Americans to our nation and beyond.

feeds.title: Chinese Association of Western Massachusetts Blog
feeds.description: Chinese Association of Western Massachusetts (CAWM) was founded about 20 years ago based on the idea that local Chinese immigrant families can celebrate traditional holidays together like it was back at home.

feeds.title: Chinese American Service League Blog
feeds.description: The CASL Blog is a website that provides information about the Chinese American Service League (CASL), a non-profit organization that provides social services to Asian Americans and other diverse populations in the Midwest.

feeds.title: Bridgewater Chinese American Association
feeds.description: The Bridgewater Chinese American Association is a non-profit organization officially registered with the U.S. government. Created in 2017 by members of the Chinese community in Bridgewater, New Jersey, the mission is to bring people of all ethnic backgrounds together and build new connections with other dedicated citizens as they move forward into a more global-thinking society.

feeds.title: Chinese American Diabetes Association
feeds.description: The Chinese American Diabetes Association (CADA) is a United States-based non-profit organization committed to advancing scientific research toward the cure of diabetes and related metabolic diseases. The mission of CADA is to provide a platform for its members to communicate and collaborate, to advance the career of its members and scientific research toward the treatment and prevention of diabetes, obesity and its complications.

feeds.title: Chinese Progressive Association
feeds.description: Founded in 1972, the Chinese Progressive Association educates, organizes and empowers the low income and working class immigrant Chinese community in San Francisco to build collective power with other oppressed communities to demand better living and working conditions and justice for all people.

feeds.title: My Chinese Home Kitchen
feeds.description: My name is Chen Jing. Welcome to my Chinese Home Kitchen! There are many kinds of Chinese cuisine, there are 8 kinds, reflecting the richness and diversity of Chinese geography and history. I am very happy to share with you Chinese cuisine and cultural traditions.

feeds.title: Asian Cooking Mom
feeds.description: In my blog, you will mostly find a variety of Asian recipes that I actually cook regularly for my family and friends. I try to make foods that are healthy, yummy, and time efficient, which are the three important factors to me after having two boys and living a busy life in the US.

feeds.title: Diana Elizabeth Blog
feeds.description: Diana Elizabeth is a Phoenix-based lifestyle blogger and photographer. Her blog covers a variety of topics, including home, garden, entertaining, style, and personal. She also shares her travel experiences and tips on how to collaborate with brands.

feeds.title: Alliance of Chinese Americans San Diego Blog
feeds.description: Alliance of Chinese Americans San Diego (ACA) is a nonprofit (501c3) organization dedicated to serving the Chinese community of San Diego. ACA assists Chinese newcomers in achieving the American Dream, by working to create and maintain an inclusive, diverse, and harmonious society.

feeds.title: Miss Panda Chinese Blog
feeds.description: Amanda 'Miss Panda' is an Intercultural Language Consultant and Trainer, the author of the 'Let's Learn Mandarin Chinese with Miss Panda!' audio album, host of the playful Chinese podcast, and presenter at the Gwaftl conference.
